sources.title: Recovered image text containing the ordinary-function and arrow-function this snippet
Tagged repository question record for the JavaScript this output question
ECMAScript 2026 EvaluateCall and property-reference thisValue rules
Deterministic Node vm validation of the recovered classic-script snippet and strict-mode boundary

claims.text: The repository OCR contains the complete snippet with window.value, fnA/fnB/fnC, objA/objB/objC, and the three calls; the candidate answers that recovered code rather than guessing from the title alone.
For objA.fn() and objB.fn(), property-reference call evaluation supplies the base object as thisValue to the ordinary function call, yielding objA and objB respectively.

Arrow-function calls do not create a new ordinary dynamic this binding; this inside the arrow resolves through the enclosing lexical environment, so fnB's arrow uses fnB's objB binding and fnC's returned arrow retains fnC's outer binding.

In the recovered non-strict classic-script boundary, the bare fnC() call receives an undefined/null-equivalent this argument that OrdinaryCallBindThis replaces with the Realm global this value, so the returned arrow later reads window.value and produces v.

If the same source is made strict, fnC's this remains undefined and the returned arrow throws TypeError when it later evaluates this.value; therefore A/B/v is not an environment-independent output claim.

Executing the exact recovered snippet in a classic-script-style Node vm context with window bound to the context global produces A, B, v in order; the same fixture independently checks the strict-mode TypeError boundary.

checks: recovered classic-script snippet outputs A, B, v in order
objB arrow uses the surrounding fnB this binding
objC stored arrow does not rebind this at the later property-call site
strict-mode variant fails at the third this.value access with TypeError

boundary_tests.expected: third invocation throws TypeError because the lexical outer this is undefined

findings: The candidate is anchored to the full recovered image-text snippet and does not infer a missing program from the canonical title.
The A and B outputs are derived from property-reference call semantics plus the lexical-this rule for the inner arrow, not from mnemonic wording.
The v output is correctly scoped to a non-strict browser classic-script boundary; the candidate explicitly rejects an unconditional environment-independent claim.
The strict-mode counterexample is executable and proves why the boundary matters.
The later objC.fn() property call is correctly distinguished from creation-time fnC(), so the answer does not mistakenly rebind the arrow to objC.
The OCR's inline expected-output comments are not used as the sole proof; the result is independently reproduced and grounded in ECMAScript 2026 semantics.
No production experience, performance metric, or browser behavior outside the recovered contract is fabricated.
Required human approval remains a separate promotion gate.
